questions.q: What was Reuben Smith's one great fault?
questions.evidence: he had one great fault and that was the love of drink

questions.q: Why was Reuben able to doctor horses almost as well as a farrier?
choices: He had lived two years with a veterinary surgeon
He had read many books about horses
questions.evidence: he had lived two years with a veterinary surgeon

questions.q: Why was Reuben dismissed the first time?
choices: He was too drunk to hold the reins after a ball
He lamed one of the earl's horses
He stole money from the earl
questions.evidence: he was so drunk that he could not hold the reins

questions.q: What did Reuben promise when he was taken back again?
choices: He would never taste another drop while he lived there
He would never ride Black Auster
He would leave in a year
questions.evidence: he would never taste another drop as long as he lived there

questions.q: What problem with Beauty's shoe did the hostler notice at the White Lion?
choices: A nail had started coming loose
questions.evidence: A nail in one of my front shoes had started

questions.q: Why did Beauty think it was strange that Smith would not have the shoe fixed?
choices: Smith was usually very careful about loose nails
questions.evidence: he was generally wonderfully particular about loose nails in our shoes

questions.q: About what time did Smith finally call for Beauty to leave the inn?
questions.evidence: it was nearly nine o'clock before he called for me

questions.q: What made Beauty stumble and fall?
choices: Galloping over sharp new stones with a shoe gone
A rabbit hole in the road
A cart coming the other way
questions.evidence: with one shoe gone, I was forced to gallop at my utmost speed

questions.q: Beauty says the road "was not much frequented." What does "frequented" mean here?
questions.evidence: The road was not much frequented

questions.q: What did Beauty think about as he stood waiting alone in the moonlight?
choices: Summer nights long ago with his mother at Farmer Grey's
questions.evidence: when I used to lie beside my mother in the green pleasant meadow at Farmer Grey's
